## Callouts

Label a figure, then cite it with `@fig-plot`. Five callout types follow.

::: {.callout-note}
Hazard ratios are adjusted for age and sex.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
Use `strata()` to relax proportional hazards.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
Small cells make the estimate unstable.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## Database lock

Do not unblind before the database lock.
:::

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}
Interim results are not for publication.
:::

## Tabsets

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{.r filename="analysis.R"}
fit <- coxph(Surv(t, e) ~ arm, data = adsl)
summary(fit)
```

### Python

```{.python filename="analysis.py"}
fit = CoxPHFitter().fit(adsl, duration_col="t", event_col="e")
```

### Julia

```{.julia filename="analysis.jl"}
fit = coxph(@formula(Surv(t, e) ~ arm), adsl)
```

:::

## Code

A code window with a long line that scrolls:

```{.r filename="long.R"}
model <- coxph(Surv(time_to_event_in_days, event_indicator) ~ treatment_arm + age_at_baseline + sex + region + baseline_score, data = analysis_data_set)
```

A code block without a window:

```r
summary(model)
```

| Arm     | Events | Hazard ratio |
|---------|-------:|-------------:|
| Placebo |     42 |         1.00 |
| Active  |     27 |         0.61 |

: Events per arm.
